extracted.intended_audience: trademark practitioners, attorneys, and providers of automated trademark-filing services (e.g., TEAS/website workflow operators)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements for preparing, signing, and filing U.S. trademark applications electronically (TEAS and other electronic workflows), including signature and verified-statement rules, practitioner duties, and related disciplinary consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO trademark electronic signature requirement (37 C.F.R. § 2.193)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person named as the signatory on an electronic trademark document filed with the Office must personally enter his or her electronic signature on the document (i.e., personally enter the combination of letters, numbers, spaces and/or punctuation marks that he or she has adopted as a signature, placed between two forward slash ("/") symbols in the signature block on the electronic submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TMEP § 611.01(c) guidance: "All documents must be personally signed. ... The person(s) identified as the signatory must manually enter the elements of the electronic signature. Another person (e.g., paralegal, legal assistant, or secretary) may not sign the name of a qualified practitioner or other authorized signatory. Just as signing the name of another person on paper does not serve as the signature of the person whose name is written, typing the electronic signature of another person is not a valid signature by that person."

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on third-party entry of electronic signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Another person (e.g., paralegal, legal assistant, or secretary) may not sign the name of a qualified practitioner or other authorized signatory; typing the electronic signature of another person is not a valid signature by that person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual entry by the named signatory is required for electronic submissions; automated insertion of characters representing another person's signature into the signature block (by a workflow) is impermissible under 37 C.F.R. § 2.193 and TMEP § 611.01(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verified-statement requirement for trademark applications (37 C.F.R. § 2.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each trademark application must include a verified statement as required by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The verified statement must contain the language provided by USPTO regulations, depending on the type of application. Verified statements must be supported by a declaration under 37 C.F.R. § 2.20 (or 28 U.S.C. § 1746) and signed in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 2.193 (see 37 C.F.R. § 2.2(n) and TMEP § 611.03(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verified-statement content for § 1(a) (37 C.F.R. § 2.33(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application under section 1(a) of the Trademark Act, the verified statement must allege specified facts about use and ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically it must allege: (1) that the applicant believes the applicant is the owner of the mark; (2) that the mark is in use in commerce; (3) that to the best of the signatory's knowledge and belief, no other person has the right to use the mark in commerce either identically or in such near resemblance as to be likely to cause confusion; (4) that the specimen shows the mark as used on or in connection with the goods or services; and (5) that the facts set forth in the application are true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verified-statement content for § 1(b) or § 44 (37 C.F.R. § 2.33(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application under section 1(b) or 44, the verified statement must allege intent and entitlement to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically it must allege: (1) that the applicant has a bona fide intention to use the mark in commerce; (2) that the applicant believes the applicant is entitled to use the mark in commerce on or in connection with the goods or services specified; (3) that to the best of the signatory's knowledge and belief, no other person has the right to use the mark in commerce either identically or in such near resemblance as to be likely to cause confusion; and (4) that the facts set forth in the application are true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and formal requirements of a verified statement (37 C.F.R. § 2.2(n); TMEP § 611.03(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A verified statement is a statement that is: (a) sworn to, made under oath or in an affidavit, or supported by a declaration under 37 C.F.R. § 2.20 or 28 U.S.C. § 1746; and (b) signed in accordance with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 2.193.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because signature requirements under § 2.193 include personal signing, a verified statement submitted without personal signature and proper declaration will not meet the definition and may be defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEAS filing: declaration and signature linkage (TEAS-specific requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verified statements in trademark applications submitted through TEAS are to be supplied by a declaration under 37 C.F.R. § 2.20 and signed pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 2.193(a)(2), (c), (d), and (e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a TEAS-prepared application, the signatory signs the trademark application, the verified statement in the application, and the declaration in support of the verified statement (i.e., all three are to be signed by the signatory in accordance with the signature rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner competence obligation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must be competent regarding USPTO trademark signature and verified-statement requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to understand adequately the USPTO trademark signature requirements (37 C.F.R. § 2.193), the TMEP guidance (TMEP § 611.01(c)), or the verified-statement requirements (37 C.F.R. §§ 2.2(n), 2.33(a), 2.33(b)) constitutes a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 (competence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candor, misrepresentation, and conduct-prejudicial standards (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.303, 11.804)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner conduct that causes filings to be prepared, signed, or filed in a manner that does not comply with signature rules or that misrepresents facts may violate candor, misrepresentation, and conduct prejudicial provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, causing trademark applications to be prepared, signed, and filed through an automated workflow that did not comply with the USPTO electronic signature rules and guidance supports findings of violations of 37 C.F.R. § 11.303(a)(1),(a)(3),(b),(d); 11.804(c); 11.804(d); and 11.804(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's opportunity to review and personally sign completed application and declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be presented with the text of the declaration supporting the verified statement and with their completed USPTO trademark application (including the declaration) prior to filing so they can personally sign as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated workflows that populate TEAS fields and file applications without presenting the completed application and declaration to the applicant and without the applicant's personal entry of the electronic signature are contrary to the USPTO signature regulations and TMEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of the federal trademark registration process
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark filings bearing verified statements supported by declarations are relied upon by the USPTO in examining applications, registering marks, and renewing registrations; filings signed contrary to electronic signature requirements adversely affect the integrity of the registration process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where filings are signed and filed contrary to the signature regulations, there may be significant adverse consequences to applicants' intellectual property rights, including potential cancellation, termination, or invalidation of applications or registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial/notification duties when noncompliant filings are discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: When filings are discovered to have impermissible signatures, practitioners/operators should notify affected applicants and provide guidance/resources about the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the stipulated facts Respondent informed each affected customer that their electronic signature did not meet USPTO rules, provided a hyperlink to TMEP § 611.01(c), and alerted customers that there may be adverse consequences (e.g., cancellation, termination, invalidation) absent a proper signature—these are presented as appropriate corrective steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible disciplinary sanctions and publication of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and signature/verified-statement requirements can result in disciplinary sanctions (e.g., public reprimand) and public publication of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes: public reprimand, electronic publication at OED's FOIA Reading Room, notice publication in the Official Gazette, and that the Office may consider the record in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings. Respondent also waived rights to seek reconsideration or appeal in this case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record as aggravating or rebutting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of the disciplinary proceeding in later matters involving the same or similar misconduct, both as an aggravating factor in determining discipline and to rebut statements by or on behalf of the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing prevents the Office from considering this record when addressing further complaints or in future disciplinary proceedings against the respondent.
